[Recording](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hKlXFFsCL_w&list=PLkifVhhWtccxt1TE7w_HbNGhY5gpDTaX7)**:

Main question: How do we want to handle the upgrade path and distinguishing how to read manifests in light of the combined data + DV entry approach? V1-V3 evolutions changed fields in an additive way but V4 is structurally different (fields moved into different levels of nesting etc).

  - We could disambiguate based on file format stored in the entry (parquet for v4 manifests, avro for older ones), but this was ruled out since it does tie us to file format in less desirable ways
  - Introduce a writer_format_version stored per entry in a manifest. Enum with 2 possibilities, 1 for Pre-V4 (readers interpret as pre-v4 if writer_format_version is missing, writers required to produce v4 for v4), 1 V4. V4 data manifests Contain the combined Data/DV entry structure

      -  V4 root can have V4 data entry, V4 root can reference delete manifest w v4 or pre-v4 equality delete (if we have a reasonable path to removing equality deletes or requiring them to be in root, then this goes away)
      - Pre-v4 data manifest can only have pre-v4 data file entries
      - Pre-v4 delete manifest can have pre-v4 equality/pos delete entries

body:
Agenda:

Steven W:

[Implementation milestone 1](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/16694#issuecomment-4699836457)

Milestone 1 keeps the v4 metadata tree at a fixed 2-level shape (root manifest → leaf data/delete manifests) and uses copy-on-write leaf rewrites for all mutations:

  - Direct data-file content_entries in the root manifest are reserved for a follow-up (small-write optimization).
  - Manifest delete vectors at the root level are reserved for a follow-up.
  - Column-file DV updates are reserved for a follow-up.

The goal is end-to-end parity with v3 commit/scan paths so v4 tables can be read and written through the existing API surface. Optimizations layer on top of this substrate in later milestones — they are independent of each other and can be built in parallel.

Amogh J:

  - DV snapshot ID and leaf manifests? The current implementation will set DV snapshot ID whenever replaced positions or deleted positions are set but I don’t think it should be. DV snapshot ID is only applicable for change detection for leaf data files. The diff DV (replaced positions + deleted positions) already implies the changes for that leaf manifest. Also dv snapshot/column file snapshot ID inheritance?
  - List<ColumnFile> vs base file + overlay list. Last time the discussion seemed to lead to preferring a list<columnfile> and having a distinction that the original base file in that list must have no fields set and must be the first element in the list. Want to confirm that’s the general consensus (will need to update the spec PR)

Agenda:

  - [Anoop Johnson](mailto:[email removed]) Decision on whether partition tuples are stored in the AMT. Decision points:

      - Equality delete matching. We *might* deprecate new equality deletes in v4, but still needs to handle upgrades.
      - Bucketed partitions: need a way to store the stats on transformed values.
      - Outcome: we will remove the partition tuple in v4 and replace with content_stats. Store source column values for monotonic transforms and for non-monotonic, store the expression (e.g. bucketing). But we will keep it temporarily for now to prevent test breakages. (parameterized tests)

- [Anoop Johnson](mailto:[email removed]) Tight bounds in column stats. Writeup: [Iceberg v4 Stats Tightness Representation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/13DbwnwKQXjvY3vRcFJo-qVAQWk-GB4zLzzYmFdPntZg/edit?tab=t.0)
  - [Amogh Jahagirdar](mailto:[email removed])

      - Spec changes:

          - Currently we have a separate dv_snapshot_id and column_file_snapshot_id. The original intent was that during any conflict validation or change detection we can do a minimal projection based on what exactly changed. However, the benefit of this separation is a little bit unclear if a reader typically needs to know both sets of changes anyways. **Could we consolidate this into a single modified_snapshot_id?**
          - Snapshot_id assignment for REPLACED entries.

              - Currently as proposed, change detection for REPLACED/MODIFIED pairs just worked off of “entries where dv_snapshot_id == current_snapshot_id OR column_file_snapshot_id == current_snapshot_id”.
              - If we have a single modified_snapshot_id, we could set replaced snapshot_id to the prev modified snapshot id (current snapshot ID if not prev modified). Then changed entries can fully work off of where snapshot_id = current_snapshot_id or modified_snapshot_id == current_snapshot_id.
          - Column Files: dropping split_offsets and format_version for column files. Format_version specifically only for manifests and stored in manifest_info
